prompt: You have $40$ meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular garden. What is the largest area, in square meters, you can enclose?
hint: Call the width $x$. The perimeter is fixed at $40$, so the length depends on $x$. Write the area as a function of $x$ alone.

hints.text: Call the width $x$. The perimeter is fixed at $40$, so the length depends on $x$. Write the area as a function of $x$ alone.
One width plus one length is half the fence, so the length is $20 - x$ and $A(x) = x(20 - x) = 20x - x^2$. Set the derivative $A'(x) = 20 - 2x$ equal to $0$.
The derivative is zero at $x = 10$, so the garden is $10$ by $10$ and the largest area is $100$ square meters.

explanation: The fence gives the constraint $2x + 2y = 40$, so $y = 20 - x$. The area is then $A(x) = x(20 - x) = 20x - x^2$.
Setting $A'(x) = 20 - 2x = 0$ gives $x = 10$. Since $A'' = -2 < 0$, this is a maximum.
The maximum area is $A(10) = 10 \cdot 10 = 100$ square meters, and the best rectangle is a square.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try some rectangles
steps: The area peaks when the sides are equal.
For a fixed perimeter, the square always wins — calculus just proves what the table suggests.
